question: What range of domain IDs is considered safe to pick if I don't want to read all the background?
reference_answer: Choose a domain ID between 0 and 101, inclusive.

question: Which durability setting makes a publisher keep messages for subscribers that join late?
answer_keys: Transient local: the publisher becomes responsible for persisting samples
reference_answer: The 'transient local' durability policy: the publisher persists samples for late-joining subscriptions.

question: In ROS 2, what replaces ROS 1 latched topics?
reference_answer: Durability 'transient local' (with any depth) gives functionality similar to latching publishers.

question: Should I use a service for a computation that takes a long time and may need to be cancelled?
answer_keys: Services should never be used for longer running processes
reference_answer: No. Services should return quickly; for long-running work that may need preemption, use an action.

question: What is an action in ROS 2?
answer_keys: long-running remote procedure call with feedback
reference_answer: A long-running remote procedure call with feedback and the ability to cancel or preempt the goal.

question: What does the 'anonymous' part of the publish/subscribe description mean?
answer_keys: doesn't generally know or care which publisher originally sent it
reference_answer: A subscriber generally doesn't know or care which publisher sent a message, so publishers and subscribers can be swapped freely.

question: Do nodes have to declare their parameters before using them?
answer_keys: a node needs to declare all of the parameters that it will accept
reference_answer: By default yes: a node must declare every parameter it accepts; allow_undeclared_parameters=true relaxes this.

question: How do nodes find each other when they start up?
answer_keys: advertises its presence to other nodes on the network with the same ROS domain
reference_answer: Each node advertises its presence to other nodes in the same ROS domain (ROS_DOMAIN_ID); they reply and connections are made.

question: What is the difference between mutually exclusive and reentrant callback groups?
answer_keys: must not be executed in parallel
reference_answer: Mutually exclusive callbacks never run in parallel; reentrant callbacks may run in parallel.

question: What severity levels can a log message have?
answer_keys: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR or FATAL
reference_answer: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR and FATAL, in ascending order.

question: What is a component container?
answer_keys: host process that allows you to load and manage multiple components at runtime
reference_answer: A host process that loads and manages multiple components at runtime in the same process.

question: What does tf2 keep track of, and for how long?
reference_answer: The relationships between coordinate frames, in a tree buffered in time, so you can transform between frames at any desired time.

question: Which middleware does ROS 2 use by default when several are installed?
answer_keys: Fast DDS is selected as the default RMW implementation
reference_answer: Fast DDS (eProsima) is the default RMW implementation.

question: Where does topic statistics publish its measurements by default, and how often?
reference_answer: To the /statistics topic, by default once per second.

question: What is a node?
reference_answer: A participant in the ROS 2 graph that uses a client library to talk to other nodes.

question: Why is ROS 2 publish/subscribe called strongly typed?
answer_keys: semantics of each field are well-defined
type is enforced at various levels
reference_answer: Field types are enforced at various levels, and each field has well-defined semantics (e.g. IMU angular velocity in rad/s).

question: How can I measure how fast messages are arriving on /turtle1/pose?
reference_answer: Run `ros2 topic hz /turtle1/pose`.

question: How do I send a goal to an action from the command line and see feedback?
reference_answer: `ros2 action send_goal <action_name> <action_type> <values>`, add `--feedback` to see feedback.

question: How can I save a node's current parameter values to a file?
reference_answer: `ros2 param dump <node_name> > file.yaml`.

question: How do I start a node with parameters loaded from a YAML file?
reference_answer: `ros2 run <pkg> <exe> --ros-args --params-file <file>`.

question: How can I give the turtlesim node a different name when I launch it?
reference_answer: Remap the node name: `ros2 run turtlesim turtlesim_node --ros-args --remap __node:=my_turtle`.

question: How do I record only two topics into a bag with my own name for it?
reference_answer: `ros2 bag record -o subset /turtle1/cmd_vel /turtle1/pose`; -o sets the bag name.

question: How do I see details about a recorded bag file?
reference_answer: `ros2 bag info <bag_file_name>`.

question: Which tool checks my ROS 2 setup for problems and prints a full report?
reference_answer: ros2doctor: `ros2 doctor --report`.

question: How do I create a new Python package with the ROS 2 CLI?
reference_answer: `ros2 pkg create --build-type ament_python --license Apache-2.0 <package_name>`.

question: How do I install all the dependencies of the packages in my workspace's src folder?
reference_answer: `rosdep install --from-paths src -y --ignore-src` from the workspace root.

question: How do I visualise the tree of coordinate frames that tf2 knows about?
reference_answer: Run `ros2 run tf2_tools view_frames`, which writes a diagram of the frame tree.

question: How can I publish a fixed transform from the command line without writing code?
reference_answer: `ros2 run tf2_ros static_transform_publisher --x .. --frame-id world --child-frame-id ..`.

question: How do I load a component into a running container?
reference_answer: `ros2 component load /ComponentManager <package> <plugin>`, e.g. composition composition::Talker.

question: How can I turn on debug output for just one node when I run it?
reference_answer: Pass `--ros-args --log-level <logger>:=DEBUG` (e.g. talker:=DEBUG).

question: How do I run only the tests of one Python package and pass arguments to pytest?
reference_answer: `colcon test --packages-select <pkg> --pytest-args -k <test_name>`.

question: How do I make colcon use symlinks so I can edit Python files without rebuilding?
reference_answer: `colcon build --symlink-install`.

question: What is the difference between an underlay and an overlay workspace?
answer_keys: Packages in your overlay will override packages in the underlay
reference_answer: An overlay is a secondary workspace on top of an underlay; the underlay must provide overlay dependencies, and overlay packages override underlay ones.

question: Where do I register my Python node's executable so ros2 run can find it?
reference_answer: In setup.py, inside the console_scripts list of the entry_points field.

question: Which CMake function generates code for my custom .msg and .srv files?
reference_answer: rosidl_generate_interfaces(${PROJECT_NAME} ...) in CMakeLists.txt.

question: How can a Python node react when parameters change, including another node's parameters?
reference_answer: Use the ParameterEventHandler class to register callbacks for parameter changes.

question: How do I switch my nodes to a different DDS vendor at run time?
reference_answer: Set the RMW_IMPLEMENTATION environment variable, e.g. RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_connextdds ros2 run ...

question: How do I stop my nodes from discovering nodes on other computers?
answer_keys: LOCALHOST means a node will only try to discover other nodes on the same machine
reference_answer: Set ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST.

question: Why does my node hang forever when I call a service synchronously inside a callback?
reference_answer: Synchronous call() inside a callback can deadlock; use call_async instead.

question: Large messages over WiFi fill up memory and stall; which kernel setting helps?
reference_answer: Reduce net.ipv4.ipfrag_time (e.g. sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_time=3).

question: How do I set up a Fast DDS discovery server and point my nodes at it?
reference_answer: Run `fastdds discovery --server-id 0` and export ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER=127.0.0.1:11811 in the nodes' terminals.

question: What do I need to run before nodes using rmw_zenoh can find each other?
reference_answer: Start the Zenoh router with `ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd`; without it nodes don't discover each other.

question: Which three environment variables turn on and enforce SROS2 security?
reference_answer: ROS_SECURITY_KEYSTORE, ROS_SECURITY_ENABLE=true and ROS_SECURITY_STRATEGY=Enforce.

question: How do I create the keystore for ROS 2 security?
reference_answer: `ros2 security create_keystore demo_keystore`.

question: When does intra-process communication avoid copying messages?
answer_keys: zero-copy will not occur in that case
reference_answer: When publishing and subscribing with std::unique_ptr; with const& or shared_ptr no zero-copy occurs.

question: What must be avoided in a real-time execution path?
reference_answer: Nondeterministic operations: page faults, dynamic memory allocation/deallocation and blocking synchronization.

question: Which joint type lets a part rotate without limits, like a turning head?
answer_keys: continuous joint, meaning that it can take on any angle
reference_answer: A continuous joint.

question: What does xacro add to URDF files?
answer_keys: xacro is a macro language for XML
reference_answer: Xacro is a macro language for XML (constants, math, macros) to shorten URDF.

question: In which formats can launch files be written?
answer_keys: can be written in XML, YAML, and Python
reference_answer: XML, YAML and Python.

question: How do I run a callback when a process started by a launch file exits?
reference_answer: Register an OnProcessExit event handler with RegisterEventHandler.

question: How do I override QoS for topics when recording a bag?
reference_answer: Pass a YAML file of per-topic QoS with --qos-profile-overrides-path.
